lines: Sequencer built from up to seven typed rules of scale-degree and duration pairs, where the last degree of a rule picks the rule that follows it, with every degree quantised to a scale set on the menu
Starts and stops the sequence, and the lamp in it is lit while the sequence runs
Restarts the sequence of every channel at the first rule
One pulse per beat drives everything; every duration written in a rule is counted in these pulses, and with nothing patched here the sequence never advances
A trigger restarts every channel at the first rule; with a cable in EVAL in Rule select mode it jumps straight to the first step of the rule that voltage picks
A trigger flips the sequence between running and stopped, exactly as the RUN button does
Steers which rule plays next, in whichever way the Eval input mode menu item is set to: a 0 to 10V rule number, a gate above 2V holding the current rule, or a trigger releasing the next transition
The pitch of the step playing on that channel, one volt per octave, quantised to the scale and root note set on the menu
10V while the step playing on that channel sounds, dropping briefly at each new step so that envelopes retrigger, and staying at 0V through a silence step
A 10V trigger when the rule playing on that channel finishes, with all of that rule's repetitions counting as one block
0V to 10V saying which rule that channel is playing, in steps of ten sixths of a volt, with 0V for the first rule and 10V for the seventh
Note — The module does nothing until a rule is typed into one of the seven text fields and a clock is patched.
Note — A rule is written as an initiator degree and duration, then an arrow, then the steps of the sequence, each a degree and a duration separated by a comma.
Note — The seven rule fields and the two random-pool fields below them are typed into directly, and confirmed with Enter or by clicking away.
Note — A rule field's bar is yellow while it has focus, red when what is typed will not parse, and green while the first channel plays that rule.
Note — Two clock pulses are needed before sub-beat timing is available; until then only the first step of each beat fires.
Note — If the clock stops or a pulse arrives late, the pitch and gate hold where they are rather than running on.
Note — Editing a rule that is currently playing takes effect only once that rule and all its repetitions have finished, so rules can be rewritten without stopping playback.
Menu — Polyphony channels — sets how many independent voices run, from one to six; all four outputs carry that many channels, and each voice makes its own random choices
Menu — Reset when starting playback — restarts the sequence every time playback is started from the RUN button or the run input
Menu — If a note has no rule...: Loop back to first rule, Jump to a random rule — sets what happens when the last degree of a rule matches no other rule's initiator
Menu — Eval input mode: Rule select (0-10V CV), Loop / Hold rule (Gate), Advance on trigger (Trigger) — sets how the EVAL jack steers the sequence
Menu — Autoreset after steps (each step = 1 beat): Off, 8 beats, 16 beats, 32 beats, 64 beats — restarts the sequence automatically after that many clock pulses
Menu — Scale — sets the scale the rule degrees are quantised to, natural major by default
Menu — Root note — sets the tonic of that scale, C by default
Menu — Random degree range (r) — sets the limits the random character picks between when the degree pool is empty, and the limits the plus and minus operators wrap at
Menu — Randomize rules style: Melodic, Acid / Techno, Ambient / Evolving, Complex L-System — sets the profile used when Randomize Rules writes the rules
Menu — Randomize Rules — writes a fresh set of rules and both random pools in the chosen style; leave the seed field above it empty for a random seed, or type one in to repeat a particular result

LSystem.notes: Read from src/LSystem.cpp, src/LSystemEngine.hpp and LSystem_manual_EN.md at commit d2a810c, the commit that carries version 2.2.2; the only later commits touch the changelog and the module's display name. The rule fields and the two random pools are custom text widgets rather than parameters, so they have no position in the census and no click on them can reach this help; they are covered by module notes instead. The RESET button and the reset input are not the same: src/LSystem.cpp:665 makes the jump-to-selected-rule behaviour conditional on the reset arriving at the jack rather than the button, so the button always performs a plain reset. The RULE output's step is the rule row index times 10 divided by 6, at src/LSystem.cpp:578, which the manual gives as about 1.667V. Two menu names differ from the manual's wording: the manual calls the autoreset item Autoreset after steps where the code prints Autoreset after steps (each step = 1 beat), and it names the randomize styles Ambient and Complex Chaos where the code prints Ambient / Evolving and Complex L-System. The names used here are the code's.

lines: Generates one voltage transition from an Init voltage to a Target voltage, timed in whole clock pulses and shaped by one of four curves
Sets the voltage the transition starts from, -10V to 10V; the setting is captured at the instant the transition starts
Sets the voltage the transition runs to, -10V to 10V; the setting is captured at the instant the transition starts
Sets how many clock pulses the transition lasts, 1 to 64 in whole steps, with the delay setting taken off the top so the two together never exceed 64
Starts a transition on the next clock edge, or at once when a clock edge has passed within the chaining window; a press is ignored while a transition or its delay is already running
Exchanges the INIT and TARGET settings
Steps the curve on by one each press, cycling Ramp, Ramp Back, Step and Triangle
Steps the start delay on by one each press, cycling OFF, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 clock pulses counted from the edge that arms the transition
Rising edges both start the transition and time it, one pulse to one step of the duration; if the clock stops the output holds where it is until the next edge
A rising edge cancels an armed, delayed or running transition and snaps the output back to the INIT voltage
A trigger starts a transition on the next clock edge, or at once when a clock edge has passed within the chaining window; it is ignored while a transition or its delay is already running
A 10V trigger 10ms long, sent when a transition finishes
The transition voltage; it holds the INIT setting until the first transition, and afterwards rests at TARGET for Ramp and Step or back at INIT for Ramp Back and Triangle
Note — Nothing happens until a clock is patched and a transition is fired, from the FIRE jack or the button. A fire before any clock edge has arrived arms the module until the first edge.
Note — Every setting is captured at the instant a transition starts, so knob, curve, delay and easing changes made during a transition or its delay apply only from the next one.
Note — The two-digit readout mirrors the DURATION setting, the DLY readout the delay setting and the icon beside them the curve; none of the three can be clicked.
Note — The yellow lamp is lit from the moment a fire is accepted until the transition ends, covering the delay as well as the transition.
Note — Only the difference between the two ease settings is used, so setting both to the same value gives the plain linear shape on every curve.
Menu — Ease in — softens the start of the motion, 0 to 100 per cent
Menu — Ease out — softens the arrival at the end of the motion, 0 to 100 per cent

Menu — Same-step chain — treats a fire arriving within half a millisecond of a clock edge, or a quarter of the last clock period where that is shorter, as falling on that edge rather than the next one

MorphfastMini.notes: Read from src/MorphfastMini.cpp and MorphFastMini_manual_EN.md at commit d2a810c, the commit that carries version 2.2.2. The Ease in and Ease out parameters, indices 7 and 8, have no widget on the panel at all: they are reached only through the module menu, where src/MorphfastMini.cpp:446 to 453 attach their parameter quantities to two sliders. They therefore get no line and no tag, and are covered by menu lines instead. The easing is a single quadratic, at src/MorphfastMini.cpp:117 to 119, whose coefficients are one minus ease-in plus ease-out and ease-in minus ease-out, which is why equal settings cancel to the linear shape. The duration ceiling at src/MorphfastMini.cpp:138 is 64 minus the delay in pulses, so a long delay shortens the longest transition available. Everything the manual states about ranges, curve behaviour, the 10ms end-of-transition trigger and the same-step window matched the source.
